headline: Deep models reconstruct 3D tissue and infer missing omics layers from sparse spatial data
label: 3D Spatial Omics Reconstruction
summary: New methods (HIM-INR, THiRST, ORBIS) lift spatial transcriptomics into 3D, while MorphoProt, CORAL and DIRAC infer or align molecular layers.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reconstructing continuous 3D tissue molecular states from sparse or non-spatial inputs. HIM-INR uses a histology-informed multi-task implicit neural representation to interpolate gene expression between sparse spatial transcriptomics sections. THiRST builds multi-resolution 3D volumes from serial 2D sections via morphology-guided registration. ORBIS goes further, using generative flow matching to reconstruct whole 3D specimens from single-cell expression without spatial references, scaling to 3.7M cells. A second thread, continued from earlier work, infers or aligns modalities. MorphoProt predicts spatial protein abundance with RNA-guided cross-attention over multiscale histology. CORAL integrates transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic and epigenomic layers through a graph-attention generative model, and DIRAC combines vertical multi-omic integration with cross-study label transfer. Separate volumetric imaging work (AstroSeg-vEM for astrocytes in volume EM, RobPicker for noise-robust cryo-ET particle picking) applies to 3D structure but not to omics. What is new is the shift from 2D section-wise integration toward volumetric, reference-free reconstruction.
